newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metra says diesel merger on track.
newsitem.headline: Metra says diesel merger on track.

text.p: Finnish engineering group Metra Oy Ab said on Wednesday the recently announced merger of its diesel unit with New Sulzer Diesel was on track and the new group to be established can start operating at the beginning of 1997.
"The merger is proceeding according to plans," Metra CEO Georg Ehrnrooth told a news conference.
The exact size of Metra's ownership in the new company, nor the size of Metra's cash payment included in the deal was not yet clear.

Metra on September 12 unveiled a tentative agreement to merge its diesel engine unit Wartsila Diesel with Italian Fincantieri's Swiss New Sulzer Diesel into a new company, in which Metra would have the majority and Fincantieri up to 15 percent.

"The actual size of Fincantieri's shareholding and Metra's cash payment ... will be based on the values of the business operations being contributed and the related financing arrangements," Metra said in September.
Metra on Wednesday released its January-August report, which showed a 395 million markka profit after financial items, up from 392 million in the year-ago period.
